Looking at my analysis again, I need to carefully reconsider whether "Entailment" or "Contradiction" is the correct answer.

The question asks: "Section 3306(c)(1) applies to Alice employing Bob for the year 2017."

Section 3306(c) defines "employment" and includes subsection (1) which specifically addresses agricultural labor:

"(c) Employment
For purposes of this chapter, the term "employment" means any service, of whatever nature,
(A) performed by an employee for the person employing him, irrespective of the citizenship or residence of either, within the United States, and
(B) performed outside the United States (except in a contiguous country with which the United States has an agreement relating to unemployment compensation) by a citizen of the United States as an employee of an American employer, except-
(1) agricultural labor unless-
(A) such labor is performed for a person who-
(i) during the calendar year or the preceding calendar year paid remuneration in cash of $20,000 or more to individuals employed in agricultural labor...
(B) on each of some 10 days during the calendar year or during the preceding calendar year, each day being in a different calendar week, employed in agricultural labor... 5 or more individuals..."

So Section 3306(c)(1) is the exception for agricultural labor. It says agricultural labor is NOT considered "employment" UNLESS the employer meets certain thresholds ($20,000 or 5 workers for 10 days).

Now the question is: "Section 3306(c)(1) applies to Alice employing Bob"

The facts:
- Alice paid Bob $3,200 for agricultural labor
- The labor was performed in Venezuela (outside US)
- Alice is an American employer
- Alice employed only Bob (one individual)

The labor was performed outside the US by an American employer, so it falls under 3306(c)(B).


Since this is agricultural labor performed abroad, 3306(c)(1) governs the analysis. Alice paid $3,200, well below the $20,000 threshold, and employed only one worker. Because she doesn't meet either requirement, the exception applies and this agricultural labor doesn't qualify as "employment" under the statute.
